Nina: heads-up — customer (acct_789) seeing sudden 429s when they burst across regions. They say requests are routed to us-east then get a 429 and client retries to eu-west which also returns 429s. Happening during scheduled batch job at 03:00 UTC. Logs attached in their report: request ids xYz123, xYz124. They say they have 5k qps short lived bursts. Can we confirm behavior for cross-region overflow? :eyes:

Evan: thanks — passing to infra. quick q: are those pure text gen calls or embedding requests?

Nina: text gen (completion=streaming) mostly, some calls include function-calling. payloads ~1.2k tokens.

Jamie: linking serving runtime: when a region exhausts capacity we have a failover policy that tries other regions but only if model variant/latency settings match. If failover is triggered rapidly during a burst, we might still hit regional unit limits and return 429s. Need the raw request headers from the customer.

Nina: they provided sample headers: ```
Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED
X-Redwood-Account: acct_789
X-Forwarded-For: 18.23.45.67
X-Region-Prefer: auto
```

Ali: can you ask them to pull an example response headers too? We emit `x-rw-region`, `x-rw-fallback`, `x-rw-rate-limit` — those will tell us where the request landed and if fallback policy executed. Also need `x-rw-req-id`.

Nina: customer just pasted one response: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-region: us-east-1
x-rw-fallback: attempted->eu-west-1
x-rw-rate-limit: user=1000/60
x-rw-req-id: xYz123
Retry-After: 3
```

Evan: ok that pattern suggests primary region hit a hard per-account QPS cap, then failover attempted but target region also returned a quota error. Two possibilities: 1) account-global quota (sum across regions) exhausted, or 2) routing hit local per-region throttle while backend hasn't accepted cross-region increase.

Thomas: from billing/quota side: acct_789 has a burst allowance but it is limited by reserved capacity + shared pool. I see they have a monthly reserved commit and a low burst headroom currently (usage spiked earlier today). I'll pull the exact numbers.

Jamie: quick repro we can run from our lab to simulate: ```bash
for i in {1..1200}; do 
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" -d '{"input":"token heavy"}' https://api.redwood/run > /dev/null &
done
wait
```
If we hit 429s and get `x-rw-fallback` cookies, that reproduces. But important: include `-H 'X-Region-Prefer: auto'` to exercise routing.

Ali: I'll run a controlled test against staging with their token-scoped rate limits and observe `x-rw-` headers. Also will check gateway logs for consistent backpressure signals and whether we returned a 429 with `Retry-After` or a gated 503.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0457 (priority P2) — paging infra on-call.

Evan: results from initial staging run: we get a burst of 429s from us-east, then ~20% of requests were routed to eu-west but they immediately returned 429s as well. Headers show `x-rw-quota-scope: account` on the 429s — looks like account-scoped limit.

Nina: customer insists their per-minute perimeter should allow the burst. Thomas, any mismatch between analytics and enforcement? Could there be eventual consistency where the quota counters are stale across regions?

Thomas: quota system uses a hybrid: local counters per region with periodic sync to a central store. Under heavy burst, local counters may be more aggressive to preserve latency and avoid oversubscription. That can produce transient rejections even if global windows still have headroom. We'll check the windowing config for acct_789.

Jamie: mitigation options for customers right now: 1) set `X-Region-Prefer: prefer=<region>` to pin to a region with reserved capacity, 2) request a temporary increase to their burst headroom (ops change), 3) use client-side client-tokens backoff with jitter and exponential retry. We should recommend #1 for predictable throughput.

Nina: sent the customer repro steps + suggestion to pin region and to include `x-rw-client-id` header for better attribution. They're asking if we can auto-failover to another region without triggering 429s — they want seamless overflow.

Evan: truly seamless overflow without 429s requires cross-region quota coordination (strong counters) or pre-warmed capacity in target region. We have eventual-consistency design on counters to avoid latency blowups; building a strong-coordinated quota adds latency and complexity. We can offer Dedicated capacity in an explicit region to guarantee throughput.

Ali: follow-ups I'm doing: - dump gateway logs for these req ids, - check central quota sync latency metrics, - run a longer (>5m) burst test with different token sizes. Will post artifacts here.

Thomas: I'll draft a temporary bump for acct_789's burst headroom and note that billing will reconcile later. Also flag that their usage pattern looks like scheduled batch work — we should propose scheduling window smoothing or queueing.

Nina: thanks team. Action items for record: Evan run latency/coordination trade test, Ali run quota-sync dig and post logs, Thomas submit temporary burst increase (notify customer), Jamie write up recommended client header usage and region pinning sample. I'll update customer after we have the log dump. :thumbsup:

Evan: noted — I'll also check if model variant mismatch could cause failover rejection (different quantization or incompatible runtime). If so, failover might explicitly decline.

ops-bot: INC-2026-0457 updated: logs attached and infra on-call acknowledged.
